note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/sign-in.reason: cinatra#2566 (epic #2564 S2) the ONE review renderer reaches the run card. The review card is now a single component rendered on all three first-party hosts (the chat thread, the run card, the review page's gate region), replacing the display-only redirect card the run panel used to draw. `agentic-run-panel.tsx` is reachable from every locked route through the agents package, so the card's closure lands on all of them: the card itself, the lifecycle-card runtime (host declaration + authoritative refetch), and the two SHIPPED review components it mounts rather than restyles (the decision bar and the gate loading/blocked states) — plus the agent-ui-protocol renderable-views barrel those read the presence matrix and state schema from, which /chat already carried and the other four did not. It cannot be narrowed away without giving up the slice's premise: the run card must draw the SAME component as the other hosts, so the run panel has to reach it, and a second lighter renderer for the run card is exactly the parallel implementation the epic deletes. Dynamic import buys nothing — the analyzer follows `import()` too. The one reduction available WAS taken: the run panel no longer imports the protocol barrel directly, it reads the one constant it needs from the card module. Counts measured with the same resolution set on both sides of the base ref (9c3ecb009, after this branch was rebased onto S3): +15 on the four routes that had not yet carried the renderable-views barrel, +6 on /chat which already did. The rebase onto S3 (#2611) did NOT change these deltas — re-measured on both sides after it — because S3's +4 lands on the SERVER-side pull/ladder modules while this card is a client component that reaches its authoritative refetch over HTTP, so the two closures do not overlap. Re-measured after the rebase onto #2618 (S4): S4's one new first-party module (packages/agent-ui-protocol/src/renderable-views/lifecycle-cards.ts) is ALREADY inside this slice's closure — the review card reads the presence matrix from the same deep specifier — so the two raises OVERLAP rather than add. The committed ceilings are the measured counts on the rebased tree, with the companion extension repos cloned pinned exactly as CI clones them, not arithmetic over the two branch deltas.
